---
title: "Criterion-specific excess risk of a common report"
subtitle: "4.5 · commonality costs from postrank, with live and archived examples"
description: "Increase in each criterion's risk relative to its own optimum in the same report family."
---

A criterion may have higher risk under a common report than it would have under grades chosen for that
criterion alone. We call the difference the commonality cost. Each connector joins the separate minimum to
the risk of the common report for that criterion. Both evaluations use the same set of possible reports and
withholding cost. Equal error weights can still give unequal costs. The larger examples use optimization
bounds saved with the original reports.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Equal weights.** The excess risks are .0490 on score A and .0145 on score B. Each connector joins the criterion-specific optimum to its common-report evaluation. The comparison table keeps each criterion’s risk separate from its wrong share.
- **Score A only.** The common report is score A’s own best, so score A has zero excess risk and score B has excess risk .1481.
  Score B still has its own comparison; a zero error weight does not remove that criterion from the display.
- **w .70.** The common report becomes {A} > {B, C, D} > {E, F}: the excess risks are .0253 on score A and .0563 on score B.
  Moving a weight changes the objective used to select the common report.
- **Score B only.** Two common reports tie. Score A has excess risk .1580 under one and .1697 under the other; score B has zero excess risk. Both common reports and both of score B’s own optima are shown, with their equal-risk tolerance.
- **Thirty sites, higher price.** The archived common report states 276 pairs. Snap’s cost is .4455, and its
  expected wrong share among those stated directions is .784. The cost interval comes from optimization bounds.
- **Thirty sites, lower price.** The common report withholds every direction, yet each criterion could prefer a
  report of its own. Costs are .0895, .0749 and .1022 for poverty, frl and snap, respectively.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The package writes this risk difference as $\Delta_k$. It measures the cost of a common report under the chosen
loss. Judging the weights or the consequences of using the report requires additional information. The
thirty-site results come from archived analyses of posterior draws. Their intervals are bounds on the minimum
from the search. We show the separate grade vectors where the archive includes them.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
cc <- postrank_commonality_cost(postrank(pr_tutorial$two, weights=c(score_A=.5,score_B=.5), tau=.2, G_max=3, backend="highs", report_card=FALSE, fragility=FALSE), backend="highs")
cc$table[, c("criterion_id", "cost_lower", "cost_upper")]
```
:::

Standalone: [common-grade-cost](../../embed/common-grade-cost.html), for example `?preset=w0&theme=dark`.
